correctness.rationale: Projection onto the three-normal convex hull proves unique clearance maximum and Gram contact test. Local geodesic coordinates yield a bounded Euclidean tangential triangle under positive multipliers, or a parabolic anisotropic blow-up under exactly two positive multipliers. The third tight side cuts the latter exactly in half. Uniform Jacobian convergence yields the asymptotics and conditional uniform laws. Independent finite-deficit integrations check all three coefficients but are not substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The question is natural: how rare are points near the uniquely deepest point of a fixed spherical triangle? Spherical geometry permits two-constraint optimal centers, unlike flat triangle intuition. The result distinguishes exponent 2 from 3/2, resolves a nontrivial critical half-coefficient, provides exact shape-dependent coefficients, and identifies marked rare-location limits, with a computable Gram phase test. This is structural, not a routine unmotivated finite computation.
